mechanism_narrative: As autumn progresses, the seasonal decline in outdoor activities, evidenced by falling PARKS mobility, will reduce overall out-of-home leisure, leading to a decrease in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite PARKS mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating a sustained preference for home-based activities, will continue to suppress engagement with retail and recreation venues, resulting in lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases significantly over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains consistently high.

mechanism_narrative: The slight but consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC over the last two weeks indicates a nascent positive momentum in consumer activity that will continue to drive modest gains over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 14 days, failing to show further improvement.

mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week dips in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT mobility suggest a renewed caution or localized disruption, which will translate into a further decrease in discretionary retail and recreation mobility over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM or TRANSIT falls by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days despite the observed dips in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The recent stagnation and slight dip in WORKPLACES mobility, after a period of recovery, signals a plateau in the return-to-office trend, which will continue to limit weekday retail and recreation footfall, keeping RETAIL_REC low over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES does not increase for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility significantly increases over the next 28 days, leading to a substantial rise in RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: As PARKS mobility declines due to seasonal cooling, people shift activities indoors. If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high, this indicates a preference for home-based indoor activities over commercial retail and recreation, thus depressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 8%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases significantly over the next 28 days while PARKS declines and RESIDENTIAL remains high.

mechanism_narrative: The observed two consecutive weeks of positive week-on-week change in RETAIL_REC, however small, suggests a building positive sentiment and underlying activity that will lead to further, albeit gradual, increases in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC shows two consecutive weeks of positive week-on-week change
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 14 days, reversing the prior positive momentum.

mechanism_narrative: The persistently low levels of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility, both significantly below baseline, indicate that structural barriers to a full return of urban activity remain, preventing any substantial recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases substantially over the next 28 days, even if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility remain deeply depressed.
